claims.text: The initial material is an as-received Cu substrate without surface treatment or coating.
An AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy powder can be deposited onto the Cu surface by cold spraying.
Cold-spray deposition at approximately 3 MPa and 800 °C can produce particle velocities of 500–600 m/s.
The process targets an AlCoCrFeNi coating thickness of approximately 150 μm.
Particle impact during cold spraying induces severe plastic deformation.
Impact-induced severe plastic deformation promotes mechanical interlocking between the AlCoCrFeNi coating and Cu substrate.
High-velocity cold-spray impact preserves the HEA microstructure.
Mechanical interlocking enhances adhesion of the HEA coating to the Cu substrate.
Preservation of the HEA microstructure allows the coating's wear-resistant properties to be imparted to the Cu matrix.
A cold-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating will significantly improve the wear resistance of Cu relative to untreated Cu.
The coating will improve surface protection of the Cu substrate.
The expected improvements apply under abrasive wear and mechanical-stress conditions.
Long-term performance under extreme thermal cycling or chemical degradation has not been established.
The quantitative improvement in wear resistance is unknown without experimental measurement.
The durability of the interfacial bond under extended cyclic loading and thermal stress is unresolved.
